Write a brief for new concept pictures.
The designer wrote: This trophy as a pendant, in the style of this pendant.
Aspect ratio: 1:1.

content.thinking: The designer wants the trophy cup from reference 1 turned into a pendant, styled like the oval pendant in reference 2. Nothing here touches the rules: a generic sports trophy, no brand, no person. The trophy gives the silhouette (a two-handled cup on a stepped base); the pendant gives the language: yellow gold, a milgrain beaded border, a small round bail, a soft engraved finish. A trophy pendant reads best front on, about 25 mm tall, with the bail on top of the cup's rim. The black base should become gold, perhaps with a beaded edge echoing the milgrain. Keep the background plain for the cut-out.

content.thinking: Four gold pendants on a plain grey ground. 1: a trophy cup with looped handles, an engraved flower, a bail on the rim. 2: a cup with a milgrain-edged oval face and a flower, scrolled handles. 3: a cup with a flower and a beaded foot. 4: a trophy in relief inside an oval medallion with a milgrain border, closer to the style reference than the brief, but nothing wrong with it. No people, no text, no logos, nothing the rules refuse.

Write a brief for new concept pictures.
The designer wrote: A pendant with a portrait of Taylor Swift engraved in the centre, like the pendant on the board.
Aspect ratio: 1:1.

content.thinking: An engraved portrait of a named, real, famous person. The rules refuse a real person's likeness without their consent, and nothing says she consented. This is not a trademark case that attestation could lift; it is a likeness, so refuse with category likeness. A calm reason, and the designer can still have the same pendant with an anonymous profile or a motif instead.
